#First need to run the library
```{r}

library(performance)
library(tidyverse)

```



#To read the dataset 
```{r}
df_Park<-read_csv("Parketal2001WBK-2.csv")
```

#To check the quality control
A histogram of Airspeed shows the range of values and whether anything looks strange, such as impossible values or gaps.
```{r}


df_Park%>% ggplot(aes(x = Airspeed)) +
  geom_histogram()

```

#Plot Airspeed vs Wingbeat amplitude (Bird 1)
```{r}
df_Park%>%
  filter(Bird_ID==1)%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Airspeed,y=Wingbeat_Amp))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_bw() + ## this part is added to get the line 
stat_smooth(method="lm")
```

#To fit the model making dataset of a bird 1 
```{r}

df_Park%>%
  filter(Bird_ID==1)%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Airspeed,y=Wingbeat_Amp))+
  geom_point()+
  xlim(0, 14)+
  ylim(40,130)+
  theme_bw()
```


#Filtering data with bird id 1

```{r}
df_bird1 <- df_Park %>%
  filter(Bird_ID == 1)

lm_wba_1 <- lm(Wingbeat_Amp ~ Airspeed,
               data = df_bird1)


```

#To check the assumption: check_model(lm_wba_1)  ## to see the model if the 4 plot is good. check_model() shows diagnostic plots for linearity, equal variance, normality of residuals and influential points. The histogram of residuals should look roughly bell-shaped.
```{r}
check_model(lm_wba_1) 
hist(lm_wba_1$residuals)
```

#To read the results: summary() gives the intercept, the slope (the change in amplitude per 1 m/s of airspeed), p-values and R². confint() gives the 95% confidence intervals for the intercept and slope. summary.aov() gives the ANOVA table (F-test). For a one-predictor model, its p-value matches the slope's p-value.

```{r}
summary(lm_wba_1)


confint(lm_wba_1)

summary.aov(lm_wba_1)

```

#Check the effect of the first data point: [-1, ] removes row 1.


```{r}
lm_wba_2 <- update(lm_wba_1, data = df_bird1[-1, ])
summary(lm_wba_1)
summary(lm_wba_2)
```

#Make predictions for a smooth line: seq() creates 100 evenly spaced Airspeed values from the minimum to the maximum.predict(..., int = "c") gives the predicted value (fit) and the confidence interval (lwr, upr) for each of those values.bind_cols() puts the airspeeds and predictions side by side in one table.

```{r}
df_newbird <- 
  tibble(Airspeed = seq(min(df_bird1$Airspeed), # the minimum of the range
                        max(df_bird1$Airspeed), # the maximum of the range
                        length = 100)) # this tells R how many values to generate


df_preds <- predict(lm_wba_1,
                    newdata = df_newbird,
                    int = "c")

df_newbird_preds <- bind_cols(df_newbird, as_tibble(df_preds))
```


#Final plot

```{r}
ggplot(df_newbird_preds,
       aes(x = Airspeed, y = fit)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr,
                  ymax = upr),
              alpha = 0.25) + # this argument makes the CI transparent
  labs(x = "Airspeed (m/s)",
       y = expression("Wingbeat Amplitude(degrees C)")) + 
  geom_point(data = df_bird1,aes(y=Wingbeat_Amp),## to get the line and points together we used this code along with the previous code. we can get any help from the 
             colour = "blue")+
  geom_line(colour = ("red")) +
  theme_bw()
```
